headline: BLNR Rejects Mahi Pono Long-Term Water License

meeting.body: BLNR Rejects Mahi Pono Long-Term Water License
meeting.summary: The state land board rejected a staff recommendation to start a long-term water license for Mahi Pono, a vice chair reported.
meeting.recap: A planned community meeting in Upcountry and Kula was canceled after a tropical storm.[[0:00:37]] That meeting will be rescheduled for September or October.[[0:00:49]] BLNR staff recommended starting the process to issue a long-term water license to Mahi Pono.[[0:01:50]] There were about 8 hours of testimony, and oral testimony was about 95% opposed.[[0:02:12]] A community member withdrew a contested case request (a formal, trial-like hearing) so the board could vote.[[0:04:49]] All six members present voted to deny the staff's recommendation.[[0:06:43]] The vice chair said this keeps alive the county's effort to take over managing the system.[[0:06:51]] About a month ago, a judge ordered BLNR to hold a contested case on the revocable permits.[[0:09:28]] BLNR unanimously let its chair appoint a hearings officer to start that contested case for 2026 and 2027 permits.[[0:09:55]] The vice chair said Mahi Pono could appeal in court the denial of its contested case request.[[0:10:26]]
decided: Members agreed with no objections to take the agenda out of order so the vice chair could present early.
meeting.next: The contested case process on the revocable permits will now start. Mahi Pono may appeal the denial of its contested case request in court within a set number of days. The vice chair's presentation was taken up next because he needed to leave early.

moments.q: Court ruling on revocable permits explained
